scope: Audit of the 40 tracked gold cases against the account-level context retrieval surface available to the assistant, plus the original conversation neighborhoods in the prepared corpus. Account-level retrieval includes surfaced user facts/preferences/constraints and recoverable historical conversation/file context; it is not a dump of platform-internal memory objects.
design_findings: Most retained cases are self-sufficient user authority and should not trigger semantic retrieval.

All nine gold cases marked as requiring contextual provenance have usable nearby conversation context; seven are resolved by the immediately preceding assistant turn and the other two within a few turns.
Account-wide semantic retrieval can corroborate a proposition but can also over-expand it with later or merely related state; it must not become authority by similarity.
Context evidence has at least two distinct roles: adopted assistant content and referent grounding. The current content_source field conflates them.
The ShipStats gold case is misclassified as adoption: the user reverses the assistant recommendation to defer ShipStats; the assistant context is needed only to resolve the deictic referent 'it'.
Vector retrieval should therefore be a fallback for unresolved distant referents/support, after deterministic nearby ancestry/context, not the primary semantic-support mechanism.
